parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead: Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of 15 kV. The electrons collide with a metal target and a spectrum of X-rays is produced.
parts.text: Explain why a continuous spectrum of energies of X-ray photons is produced.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the wavelength of the highest energy X-ray photon produced.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A beam of X-rays has an initial intensity *I*₀. The beam is directed into some body tissue. After passing through a thickness *x* of tissue the intensity is *I*. The graph in Fig. 11.1 shows the variation with *x* of ln (*I*/*I*₀).

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: Determine the linear attenuation (absorption) coefficient *μ* for this beam of X-rays in the tissue.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the thickness of tissue that the X-ray beam must pass through so that the intensity of the beam is reduced to 5.0% of its initial value.

figures.caption: Fig. 11.1
figures.alt: A graph of ln (I/I₀) against x, with a straight line decreasing from 0 at x = 0 cm to about −2.3 at x = 11 cm.
